title: You Need Sponsorship? Probably Not | Work In The UK Without Sponsorship
description:
You Need Sponsorship? Probably Not | Work In The UK Without Sponsorship


Thousands of international candidates get auto-rejected every year for visa sponsorship they don't actually need. If you are on a Graduate Visa, you have 2 years of unrestricted UK work rights with zero sponsorship required, and most hiring managers don't understand that. This video breaks down the sponsorship question on application forms, how to answer it, and the UK work visa routes that need no employer sponsor at all.

It is for international candidates and Graduate Visa holders who keep getting filtered out before a human reads their CV. You will leave knowing exactly how to stop self-rejecting and how to push back when a recruiter says "we can't sponsor".


What you'll learn in this video:
- Why the "do you need sponsorship" checkbox auto-rejects you before a human sees your CV
- What a UK Graduate Visa actually is: 2 years unrestricted work, zero employer cost
- The exact script to answer the sponsorship question on an application form
- A word-for-word message to push back when a recruiter says they can't sponsor
- 3 more UK work visa routes that need no employer sponsor (HPI, Global Talent, Youth Mobility)


VIDEO CHAPTERS:
0:00 You got rejected for sponsorship you didn't need
0:29 The application form trap
0:56 What a Graduate Visa actually is
1:24 What it costs the employer (nothing)
1:56 How to answer the sponsorship question
2:40 The exact pushback script for recruiters
3:10 What "we can't sponsor" really means
4:09 3 routes that need no sponsor at all
4:54 Check gov.uk for your route


If you want help positioning yourself so the visa stops ending your applications, come and join us.

WORK WITH ME:
Join my free community: https://community.offeraccelerator.co.uk/join?invitation_token=31dd2c6ff3c2d29110be25aace66bb325cab07f2-68a0b5d6-d377-438f-bb72-6e0ede239116&utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=stop-saying-you-need-sponsorship


CONNECT WITH ME
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/olivercordingley
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/olivercordingley


WATCH NEXT:
Your CV is Why You're Not Getting Hired


ABOUT ME:
I dropped out of university at 19 to build recruitment software and ATS systems used by hiring teams. For years I spoke to hundreds of hiring managers and recruiters every day, learning exactly how candidates get filtered, shortlisted, and hired from the inside. I started coaching friends through their job search using what I'd seen, then raised investment, built a software company, and hired my own team. I've seen hiring from every angle.

Today I help job seekers land offers faster using a proven 3-step system. I've coached hundreds of candidates into roles at firms like JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Deloitte, EY, and PwC and many more.

transcript: You got rejected for needing a visa sponsorship, and the truth is is that you probably didn't even need it. Now, I speak to international candidates every single week who are who are basically ticking that box on the application form before you apply for a job that basically quietly bins them before a human ever even reads their CV. And the problem is is that most of them are doing it when they don't even have to in the first place. So, in this video, I'm going to show you exactly what's going on, how you should actually answer that, you know, sponsorship question, and then also the routes that mean that no employer ever has to sponsor you at all. So, let's start with the trap because almost every application form these days has a version of it. It's basically they ask you, "Do you require sponsorship to work in the UK now or in the future?" And you kind of read that and you think, "Yeah, well, technically." And then you tick yes. And on a lot of these ATS systems, ticking yes is an instant filter, and you're gone. And not because you're not good enough, but because that one checkbox that is a knockout question. Now, here's the part that nobody actually explains to you. So, for example, if you are on a graduate visa, you don't need sponsorship right now, like not at all. So, let me break down what a graduate visa actually is because most candidates it. Now, you probably know like a graduate visa is going to give you 2 years of completely unrestricted work in the UK. And that's three if you're doing a PhD. And you can work on any job at any company at any salary on exactly the same basis as a British citizen. And there is literally no restrictions on what you can do. And here's the bit that really matters for the employer. So, to hire you, they have to do literally nothing. Like, they don't need that sponsorship license. They don't need to pay the immigration skills charge. They don't fill in any Home Office paperwork. They don't have to hit on any sort of minimum salary. So, there's no cost, and there's no admin on their side at all. So, for those 2 years, you're completely normal to them. And you've probably already paid it yourself. Like, you've paid the Home Office thousands of pounds before you even walked into that interview. So, yeah, like when you tick the box, "Yes, I need a sponsorship," you're handing the employer a problem that doesn't actually exist. So, then how should you really answer the question? So, the honest truth is this. On a graduate visa, you don't need sponsorship now, but you obviously will need it later after you stay beyond those 2 years. And most forms, what they do is they squash all of that into one yes or no tick box, so then there's no real clean answer. So, don't let the form speak for you. So, if there's a free text box anywhere, you need to write something like this. I have the full right to work in the UK for the next 2 years on a graduate visa with no sponsorship required. Now, if it is a hard yes or no with with no nuance at all, then your job is to get in front of a human before that checkbox decides your fate. So, apply and then get yourself in front of someone and have the conversation once they actually want you. And then when a recruiter or hiring manager does come back with you saying, "Sorry, we can't sponsor." you push back and you do it calmly and with facts. So, here's almost word for word what I teach my candidates to say. So, just to check before I take myself out of the process, when you say you can't sponsor, are you aware that I'm on a graduate visa? Because that comes with 2 years of full UK work rights with no sponsor license needed on your side. There's no fees. There's no paperwork. And I'm happy to send over the government guidance if that helps. And that one message has put three of my candidates straight back into the processes that they've already been written off when it comes on the form. Because here's what we can't sponsor usually like actually means. So, there's three versions of it and you need to work out which one you're sort of dealing with. So, the first one, and this is by far the most common, is that the employers simply don't understand, you know, what the visa actually is. And what they do is they hear international in their brain and then they assume that loads of paperwork and sponsorship. And that's kind of fixed with a single sentence from you. Now, the second version is that they don't want to deal with what happens after your 2 years are up. Now, that is a real concern, but it's a future conversation, not a reason to reject you today. And honestly, most roles never even get to that 2-year point anyway. The average tenure for employment is currently declining. And honestly, like most roles with British citizens don't even get to that point of that 2-year mark anyway. So, the third one is that they've got like a blanket sort of UK citizens only policy. And that one you can't really talk your way around it. But, at least now that you know to stop pouring your energy in there and then put it somewhere else that will actually pay off. So, your whole job is to figure out fast like which of these three are you actually looking at and stop letting the first one quietly cost you jobs. Now, back to that graduate visa example, which is obviously the most common route, it's not the only one where an employer has to sponsor you. And if you're earlier in this or you're planning ahead, you really need to know that these exist. So, firstly, there's a high potential individual visa. So, if you've graduated from university on the government's eligible global list in the last few years, then you can get a work visa with no employer and no sponsor behind it at all. There's also the global talent visa. So, if you've genuinely got a strong track record in tech, science, or the arts, this one doesn't need a sponsor and it can lead to permanent settlement faster than most people actually realize. And then there's also the youth mobility scheme. So, if you're from an eligible country and you're in that right age bracket, then you can come and work in the UK for 2 years. Again, with no employer sponsorship needed. Now, I'm deliberately not going to sit here and just quote you the exact fees, ages, and thresholds because they change from year to year. And the last thing I want you to do is act on a number that's probably a year out of date. So, the one thing I want you to do is this. Go to the gov.uk website, search the route that applies to you, and read it straight from the source. Because the real lesson here isn't about like any sort of single visa. It's that you've been handling employers a reason to reject you and half the time it's not even true. Because again, you're not the problem. It's that check box on the application form. So, stop letting it answer for you. Now, if this is exactly the spot that you're stuck in and you want to help position yourself so the visa stops being the thing that just ends your applications, I run a free community where I go deep on this stuff. Now, the link is down below in the description and you can come and join us. And if you know someone who keeps getting rejected over sponsorship, then send them this video as well. It might be the thing that finally changes how they apply.
